sources.headline: Lawyer for one of Cornell 7 calls for special prosecutor to be removed over previous comments
sources.text: A lawyer for one of the seven men accused of participating in a Cornell University gang rape has called for the special prosecutor on the case to recuse herself over past public comments.The lawyer had said a social media post from New York Attorney General Letitia James throws into question her investigation's "integrity and independence".In the 28 September post, James wrote that "what this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable" and told survivors that "we stand with you".The university's administration is under fire over its alleged mishandling of the October 2024 incident and, according to US media, now faces a no-confidence vote by Cornell faculty. The university's Faculty Senate, a governing body comprised of professors and other academic staff, will vote on a resolution of no confidence next week, according to reports. Cornell is an Ivy League university, alongside Harvard and Yale, and its faculty includes Nobel laureates and other distinguished researchers.A majority no-confidence vote would be a largely symbolic gesture, signalling the broader faculty's discontent and applying pressure on university leadership to act.Cornell University announced on Tuesday that it was hiring Sally Yates, a former deputy attorney general, to lead an independent review of the university's practices and procedures on sexual assault and related conduct."Yates and her team will conduct a detailed review of the University's response to the allegations involving Jane Doe", the university said in a statement, "including whether Cornell followed its policies and procedures in responding to the matter".Allegations made in a lawsuit against seven men and the university have rocked the campus in New York state, with hundreds of students and faculty members gathering there on Monday in protest, and sparked anger across the country.New York Governor Kathy Hochul last week appointed James as a special prosecutor to investigate the case and how law enforcement and the university initially responded to the allegations made by a woman identified in the lawsuit as Jane Doe.Jane Doe has accused the university of failing to protect her, after she was allegedly drugged and raped by the men for several hours at a fraternity party. Days before she was appointed special prosecutor, James wrote on X: "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. "I'm holding her in my heart and in my prayers," she continued. "To her, and to all survivors: you're not alone. We stand with you."The lawyer for one of the seven accused said these remarks were disqualifying. In a statement sent to the BBC's US media partner, CBS News, the lawyer said her comments conflict with the need for "independently evaluating the evidence"."This is not an accusation that Attorney General James is corrupt, acting in bad faith or incapable of performing her duties professionally," the statement said. "Nor am I suggesting that a court has determined that she is legally disqualified. The point is much narrower: an avoidable question now hangs over this investigation, and voluntary recusal would remove it."Governor Hochul and James were questioned about impartiality concerns during a news conference, and Hochul said James would "follow the facts". "She'll examine the evidence and go wherever it leads, and if the evidence supports charges, she will pursue them," Hochul said.

sources.headline: Cornell names Sally Yates to review university’s response to rape case
sources.text: Yates will examine Cornell’s sexual assault investigations, disciplinary process and campus police response.Cornell University trustees have named former United States Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates to conduct an independent internal review of how the university handles allegations of sexual assault and harassment, following widespread criticism over its response to a former student’s rape allegations.The trustees announced on Tuesday that Yates will examine how Cornell investigates reports of sexual misconduct and assault, its disciplinary procedures, campus police responses and the university’s oversight of fraternities.Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Cornell president vows transparency amid outrage over fraternity rape caselist 2 of 3Cornell case puts New York’s progressive image at odds with its rape lawslist 3 of 3‘Smash the patriarchy’: Activists graffiti Cornell hall over gang rape caseend of listYates served as deputy attorney general during the administration of former President Barack Obama and as acting attorney general at the start of Donald Trump’s first presidency. Trump fired her in 2017 after she directed Justice Department lawyers not to defend his initial travel ban that targeted Muslim-majority countries.“It is imperative that Cornell be willing to examine itself with the same rigor we expect of others,” Cornell Board of Trustees Chair Anne Meinig Smalling said in a statement.The appointment comes after renewed criticism of Cornell’s handling of allegations made by a woman, identified in court filings as Jane Doe, who said she was sexually assaulted by multiple members of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024.The case resurfaced after Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the university, the fraternity and seven former students in September.No criminal charges have been filed in the case. Cornell has said it expelled some students and suspended others who were accused following its own investigation, while the Chi Phi chapter was shut down.Cornell students rally against the university’s handling of allegations that a student was sexually assaulted at a fraternity house in 2024, in Ithaca, New York, on October 5, 2026 [Spencer Platt/Getty Images via AFP]“We don’t have all the answers, but we are committed to investigating and finding the answers our community deserves,” Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said in a video message on Saturday.Yates, now a partner at the law firm King & Spalding, conducts independent investigations and previously led a 2022 investigation into sexual abuse and misconduct in the National Women’s Soccer League that found systemic failures.New York Attorney General Letitia James is separately conducting a criminal investigation into the allegations after Governor Kathy Hochul appointed her special prosecutor last week.Hochul had called for an independent review of Cornell’s handling of the case amid criticism from students, faculty and others.

sources.headline: Cornell hires ex-Justice Dept official Yates to review rape claims response
sources.text: Oct 6 - Cornell University has hired a top former US Justice Department lawyer for an internal investigation of how it handled a student's allegations that she was gang-raped, a case that has brought mounting scrutiny and triggered student protests at the Ivy League school.Sally Yates, who served as deputy US attorney general from 2015 to 2017, will conduct an independent review of how Cornell prevents and responds to sexual assault claims, university officials said on Tuesday.The investigation by Yates, now a partner at law firm King & Spalding, will include a “detailed review” of Cornell’s response to the student's claims that she was sexually assaulted by multiple men during a fraternity party in October 2024.The student, referred to as Jane Doe in a lawsuit she filed against Cornell and seven fraternity members, has said the Ithaca, New York university failed to adequately investigate and punish the fraternity members involved.Other Cornell students staged a mass rally on Monday voicing solidarity with Jane Doe and demanding that the school take firmer action against sexual violence on campus.A newly formed Special Committee of the Cornell University Board of Trustees said Yates will have “full independence” to conduct her review.A lawyer for Jane Doe, Thomas Giuffra, did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Tuesday about the investigation.Yates was previously hired by the US Soccer Federation to investigate allegations of sexual abuse and misconduct within the National Women's Soccer League.'DEFINING MOMENT'Cornell University President Michael Kotlikoff on October 3 called the alleged sexual assault case a “defining moment” and said the university "must do better."In her lawsuit, filed last month, Jane Doe said she was plied with drugs and alcohol and then sexually assaulted by several members of the campus chapter of the Chi Phi fraternity in October 2024 after she had become incapacitated.She had reported the alleged assault to police several weeks after the fact, leading to an internal university investigation and a law enforcement probe, but the local prosecutor declined to bring criminal charges.Cornell, which has defended its response to the original report, shut down the Chi Phi chapter and imposed a range of discipline on the fraternity members involved, including expulsions and other sanctions. REUTERS

sources.headline: Woman at centre of Cornell gang rape lawsuit targeted with threats, lawyer says
Jane Doe threatened in Cornell University rape case, lawyer says
sources.text: Topic:Sexual OffencesPosted Mon 5 Oct 2026 at 7:32amMon 5 Oct 2026 at 7:32amPeople have threatened to silence Jane Doe in the Cornell University case, her lawyer says. (AP: Heather Ainsworth)In short:The woman identified as Jane Doe in the Cornell University case has been threatened to silence, her lawyer says.Jane Doe alleges that she was drugged and raped by seven Cornell University students in 2024.Since the lawsuit was filed last month, prosecutors in New York have been criticised for their initial handling of the allegations.The woman who has alleged that she was drugged and raped by several Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer says.Thomas Giuffra, who represents the woman identified as Jane Doe, has told CNN that people have threatened to silence or harm her if she does not withdraw her civil lawsuit."She's received multiple threats," Mr Giuffra said on CNN's State of the Union.Her lawyer said he had also been threatened."I'm not afraid of these people," he said."But the threats, the abuse to protect what's going on, the status quo — these guys are disgusting. They should stay in their mother's basement and stay out of the world."The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University in Ithaca. (AP: Heather Ainsworth)Cornell president vows 'serious look' at fraternitiesIn a video, Cornell University president Michael Kotlikoff said that the university would examine the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following the outcry over the school's handling of the 2024 rape allegations."At their best, these organisations can provide students with friendship, belonging, mentorship and a powerful sense of community," he said."But being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."Since the lawsuit was filed last month, prosecutors in New York have been criticised for their initial handling of the allegations in 2024.New York Governor Kathy Hochul last week named state Attorney-General Letitia James as special prosecutor to look into the case.US President Donald Trump, a critic of Ms James for years, lambasted the decision to appoint her."And I feel badly for whoever she's looking at because they won't get a fair shake," Mr Trump told reporters on Friday.Asked about the president's comment, Mr Giuffra said the case should not be politicised."It has nothing to do with politics," he said.Reuters

sources.headline: Cornell sexual assault case: Woman at centre of rape allegations got threats to withdraw lawsuit, lawyer says
sources.text: A student walks by a sign at the entrance of Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. (File Photo)A woman who has alleged that she was drugged and raped by several Cornell University fraternity members has been threatened with harm if she does not withdraw her civil lawsuit, her lawyer said on Sunday.Thomas Giuffra, who represents the woman identified as "Jane Doe", told CNN that she had received multiple threats aimed at forcing her to drop the lawsuit, which alleges that several members of the Chi Phi fraternity drugged and sexually assaulted her in 2024."She's received multiple threats," Giuffra said on CNN's "State of the Union". He said he too had been threatened.Giuffra said the threats were an attempt to protect the status quo surrounding the case. "I'm not afraid of these people," he said, while describing those behind the threats as people trying to prevent scrutiny of what happened.The allegations have triggered renewed scrutiny of Cornell's handling of the case, as well as the actions of local prosecutors who initially did not pursue criminal charges. The woman filed the civil lawsuit in September against seven fraternity members, Cornell University, the Chi Phi fraternity and other defendants.The case dates back to October 2024, when Jane Doe, then a Cornell student, alleged that she was given alcohol, marijuana and ketamine at the Chi Phi fraternity house before being sexually assaulted after becoming incapacitated. The accused men have denied wrongdoing, with some saying the sexual activity was consensual.New York AG takes over Cornell rape investigationThe handling of the allegations has come under fresh scrutiny after reports revealed discrepancies between the woman's detailed account to campus police and the shorter sworn statement that was provided to prosecutors.In one interview with police, she reportedly told investigators that she was certain she had been raped, but that assertion was not included in the statement sent to prosecutors.Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten had initially declined to pursue charges in 2024. After the civil lawsuit triggered renewed attention, he reopened the criminal investigation and said his office would present evidence to a grand jury for possible indictment.However, New York Governor Kathy Hochul later said she had "lost faith" in the Tompkins County DA's ability to fairly oversee the case. She appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor, meaning James' office will now oversee the criminal investigation.Hochul has also criticised the initial handling of the allegations by Cornell police and local prosecutors, saying the woman had been failed by institutions that were supposed to protect her.Cornell President Michael Kotlikoff said on Saturday that the university would review the role of fraternities and sororities on campus following the public outcry. He said such organisations could provide students with friendship and community, but "being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility."US President Donald Trump has criticised the decision to appoint James, saying the people she investigates would not get a "fair shake". Giuffra, however, said the case should not be turned into a political issue."It has nothing to do with politics," he said.
